subject: Post-demo: network perimeter & data handling clarifications
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
To: Amanda Lewis <amanda.lewis@clearedgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: network perimeter & data handling clarifications

Hi Amanda — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side after the demo: 

- Scope: ClearEdge is evaluating a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood to process clinical notes (PHI/PII) for inferencing. You called out three main controls: data residency in us-east-1, short-term retention of inference artifacts, and strict egress controls.
- Ask: To keep momentum, can you confirm the list of endpoints that will be allowed outbound from the VPC (egress allowlist) and whether your environment supports establishing an AWS VPC endpoint to Redwood's ingest gateway?
- Deliverable: I attached a lightweight network sketch that shows how we typically place a private control plane + inference nodes inside a customer VPC (attachment: network_perimeter_sketch.png). This is a living sketch — we can adapt it to Pinecrest environment.

Next steps I propose:
1) Amanda / Security: provide an initial egress allowlist and any firewall/IDS constraints we should model (target: Tue, Dec 1).
2) Redwood: share SOC2 summary + our standard retention options and a short doc on KV cache handling (attached).
3) Optional: run a brief canary verification in your staging VPC once we agree on routing (tbd).

I'll loop Ben on the procurement items and Laura to coordinate the SOC2 evidence handoff. If anything above is incorrect or you'd like us to add a network capture/packet-flow sample, let me know.

Thanks,

Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: network_perimeter_sketch.png (image/png), redwood_soc2-summary.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Amanda Lewis <amanda.lewis@clearedgehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
Cc: security@clearedgehealth.com, procurement@clearedgehealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: network perimeter & data handling clarifications

Priyom — great demo, thanks. A few clarifying items from Security and Procurement after our internal sync: 

1) Data types: we will be sending de-identified and identified clinical notes to Redwood depending on the workload. Anything marked PHI must not leave our us-east-1 tenancy or be stored beyond 48 hours post-inference (exceptions require audit).
2) Egress: our security team will only permit outbound connections to a fixed IP set or via an AWS PrivateLink endpoint; NAT egress out to the public internet is disallowed in our production VPC.
3) Logging/forensics: we require audit logs that include per-request identifiers and token-level counts retained for 90 days; we also need KV cache evictions to be auditable.
4) Air-gapped constraint: full air-gap is not possible; however, for certain projects we can provision a segmented staging VPC with strict ingress/egress rules.

Action items from our side: we will run the allowlist exercise and provide the list of permitted IPs and PrivateLink requirements by Thu, Dec 3. Security will also fill the attached questionnaire (see pinecrest-questionnaire-completed.xlsx) and return it.

One question: does Redwood support an inbound-only PrivateLink pattern (Redwood nodes initiated from inside our VPC with no inbound public endpoints)? If not, we need to scope a proxy pattern with tight NAT and egress controls.

—Amanda
Amanda Lewis
Director, Cloud Architecture | ClearEdge Health
amanda.lewis@clearedgehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-2233

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
To: Amanda Lewis <amanda.lewis@clearedgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: network perimeter & data handling clarifications

Amanda — thanks for the detailed notes, really helpful. Short answers inline and a couple of asks below.

- PHI residency: we can pin inference nodes and ephemeral storage to us-east-1; control plane metadata can live in Redwood's control plane but we offer an on-prem control plane option for fully customer-managed metadata if required.
- Egress / PrivateLink: Redwood supports AWS PrivateLink for customer VPCs. We can operate in an inbound-only model: Redwood ships a light connector that initiates outbound connections to our ingestion endpoint over TLS to a customer-configured PrivateLink. That means no inbound public endpoints into your VPC. I'll attach a diagram variation for that pattern.
- Logging & retention: default request/audit logs (per-request ID, timestamp, model variant) are configurable; token-level counts can be recorded and exported to your CloudWatch or S3 with 90-day retention. KV cache eviction events are logged by the runtime and can be delivered to your SIEM via our event forwarder.

Two asks from us: 
1) Can Security add an example of the PrivateLink interface CIDR range so we can validate the connector configuration?
2) For the canary run: please confirm whether staging VPC has a bastion/NAT gateway we can use for egress-only connectivity (we prefer PrivateLink + endpoint).

I've attached the updated sketch (network_perimeter_sketch.png) and our SOC2 summary (redwood_soc2-summary.pdf). Ben — looping you for commercial handoffs and Laura for evidence exchange.

Best,
Priyom

Attachments: network_perimeter_sketch.png (image/png), redwood_soc2-summary.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks — this addresses our high-level questions and aligns with our constraints. Quick status update from our side: 

- Security provided the PrivateLink CIDR & interface requirements (attached in the questionnaire).
- Procurement wants to review a short SOW for the staging canary. I put a DocuSign test link in case we need to sign a mutual NDA before the canary kick-off.
- On the canary: staging VPC has a NAT gateway but procurement would prefer PrivateLink. We can provision an endpoint — security will share the endpoint config and an RFC for approval by Fri, Dec 4.

Next steps: 
1) Redwood: send a short SOW draft for the canary (1–2 pages) and confirm whether the PrivateLink inbound-only connector requires any special IAM roles on our side.
2) ClearEdge: we'll finalize the allowlist and PrivateLink details by Fri, Dec 4 and return the questionnaire with a couple of redlines where noted.

I'll attach the completed questionnaire and the PrivateLink details in a follow-up mail to procurement. Thanks all — leaning toward a staged canary next week if we can get the SOW and networking bits in place.

Amanda
